chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period of the woman with irregular menstruation (mustahadha) who does not purify is three months, and the waiting period of the woman who menstruates and whose menstruation becomes regular is three quru', and the qur' is the gathering of blood between two menstruations.

key_terms.الْقُرْءُ: The period of blood between two menstruations
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: Woman with irregular menstruation who does not have a fixed cycle
key_terms.قُرُوءٍ: Plural of qur', referring to periods of blood or days of purity associated with menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman with irregular menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar delineates the transitional legal status of the mustahadha, distinguishing between the three-month waiting period for those with no established cycle and the three-qur' period for those whose menstruation stabilizes. It provides the essential jurisprudential definition of the 'qur'' as the interval of blood between two distinct menstruations, a key concept in Shia fiqh for determining purity and prayer obligations. This ruling reflects the practical application of distinguishing between irregular bleeding and true menstruation, ensuring women can correctly observe their religious duties.
